questions.text: The FIRST STAGE of documentation in the insurance process is:
questions.explanation: The PROPOSAL FORM is the FIRST STAGE of the insurance documentation process. It is through the proposal form that the insured provides all necessary information about the subject matter to be insured. All other documents come after the proposal form.

questions.text: The declaration at the END of the proposal form is signed by:
questions.explanation: The insurance company usually adds a declaration at the END of the proposal form, and this declaration is SIGNED BY THE INSURED. It confirms that all the information provided in the form is true, complete, and accurate.

questions.text: The Insurance Agent in the documentation process is best described as:
options: The Final Underwriter who approves all policies
An Intermediary between insurer and insured, and the Primary Underwriter
questions.explanation: The Insurance Agent acts as an INTERMEDIARY between the insurer and the insured. The agent is also called the PRIMARY UNDERWRITER or FIELD UNDERWRITER because they collect all information from the customer and fill the proposal form — the very first step of the underwriting process.

questions.text: The process of scrutinizing the proposal form and deciding about acceptance is known as:
questions.explanation: UNDERWRITING is the process of thoroughly examining (scrutinizing) the proposal form and deciding whether to accept the risk, at what premium, and on what terms and conditions. It is a critical step in the insurance process that happens after the proposal form is submitted.

questions.text: As per IRDAI guidelines, an insurance company must process an insurance proposal within:
questions.explanation: As per IRDAI guidelines, an insurance company must process an insurance proposal within 15 DAYS of receipt. This ensures timely service to the prospective policyholder and prevents undue delays in issuing insurance coverage.

questions.text: Premium in an insurance contract is best defined as:
options: The claim amount paid to the insured
The surrender value of the policy
The maturity amount of the policy
The consideration and price paid by the insured to the insurer
questions.explanation: PREMIUM is the CONSIDERATION — the price paid by the INSURED to the INSURER for insuring the subject matter under the insurance contract. It is the insured's part of the exchange in the contract.

questions.text: Through which of the following modes can premium NOT be received?
questions.explanation: Premium CANNOT be received through a PROMISSORY NOTE. Valid modes of premium payment include cash, cheque, credit card, and online/digital payments. A promissory note is not an accepted mode of insurance premium collection.

questions.text: The maximum limit of liability of the insurer under a policy is:
questions.explanation: The MAXIMUM LIMIT of the insurer's liability under any policy is the SUM INSURED. The insurer cannot be required to pay more than this amount regardless of the actual loss. The sum insured is the ceiling on the insurer's financial obligation.

questions.text: Material Fact in an insurance proposal is important because it:
options: Helps the insured get a discount on premium
Influences the decision of the Underwriter
Is required only for life insurance proposals
Helps the insured choose the best plan
questions.explanation: MATERIAL FACT is important because it INFLUENCES THE DECISION OF THE UNDERWRITER. Complete and correct information about the subject matter helps the underwriter decide whether to accept the risk, at what premium, and on what terms. Incomplete or false material facts can void the insurance contract.

questions.text: A Fire Insurance Proposal requires information about which of the following?
options: All of the above — process of manufacturing, details of materials, and construction of building
questions.explanation: A FIRE INSURANCE PROPOSAL requires ALL THREE types of information: (1) Process of manufacturing, (2) Details of materials contained/stored in the premises, and (3) Construction of the building. All three are necessary to assess fire risk accurately.

questions.text: A Cover Note is issued when:
options: The preparation of the policy document is still pending
The insured wants to cancel the policy
questions.explanation: A COVER NOTE is a temporary document issued when the preparation of the full POLICY DOCUMENT IS STILL PENDING. It provides immediate evidence that the insurance contract has commenced, protecting the insured even before the final policy is issued.

questions.text: Cover Notes are GENERALLY used in which type of insurance?
questions.explanation: Cover Notes are generally used in MARINE INSURANCE and MOTOR INSURANCE. In these types of insurance, immediate coverage is often needed while the full policy is being prepared, making the temporary cover note essential.

questions.text: A document that provides FORMAL EVIDENCE that the insurance contract has commenced is called:
questions.explanation: The POLICY DOCUMENT is the formal document that provides evidence that the insurance contract has commenced. It is the main contract document containing all terms, conditions, coverage details, and obligations of both parties.

questions.text: WARRANTY in an insurance policy is:
options: A separate document given along with the policy
A condition expressly stated in the policy that must be complied with
The renewal notice sent by the insurer
questions.explanation: WARRANTY is a CONDITION that is EXPRESSLY STATED within the policy document itself. It must be literally complied with for the validity of the contract. It is NOT a separate document — it is embedded within the policy. Non-compliance with a warranty can render the insurance contract void.

questions.text: The Certificate of Motor Insurance should always be:
options: Kept in the vehicle at all times
questions.explanation: The Certificate of Motor Insurance must always be KEPT IN THE VEHICLE (car, bike, etc.) at all times. It serves as proof of valid insurance when checked by traffic police or other authorities. Failing to carry it is a legal violation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
